title: Stone Game VII
summary: Alice and Bob play a game with n stones in a row.
statement: Alice and Bob play a game with n stones in a row. Each turn, a player removes the leftmost or rightmost stone and scores points equal to the sum of the remaining stones. Alice aims to maximize the score difference, while Bob tries to minimize it. Given the values of the stones, determine the score difference if both play optimally.
constraints: Removing an endpoint scores the sum left behind; both players optimize final score difference.
hints: A state is the best score difference the current player can force on one interval.
Try removing either endpoint: gain the remaining sum, then subtract the opponent’s optimal difference.
Fill interval DP from width two upward and take the maximum of the two endpoint transitions.
The recurrence enumerates both legal moves and zero-sum turn exchange changes the next state’s advantage sign.
editorial: The recurrence enumerates both legal moves and zero-sum turn exchange changes the next state’s advantage sign.

tests.explanation: Optimal endpoint choices give Alice a final advantage of six.
Optimal play gives a difference of one hundred twenty-two.
